hints.title: Problem Analysis
hints.text: Count total employees in each department using grouping by dep_id.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Identify departments whose count equals the maximum count using a subquery or CTE.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy
hints.text: Join back with Employees where position = 'Manager' to retrieve manager names.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH DepartmentCount AS (
    SELECT 
        dep_id, 
        COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM Employees
    GROUP BY dep_id
)
SELECT 
    e.emp_name AS manager_name, 
    e.dep_id
FROM DepartmentCount dc
JOIN Employees e 
    ON dc.dep_id = e.dep_id 
    AND e.position = 'Manager'
WHERE dc.cnt = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM DepartmentCount)
ORDER BY e.dep_id ASC;
```

import pandas as pd

def find_manager(employees: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    dept_sizes = employees.groupby('dep_id').size().reset_index(name='cnt')
    max_size = dept_sizes['cnt'].max()
    max_depts = dept_sizes[dept_sizes['cnt'] == max_size]['dep_id']
    managers = employees[(employees['dep_id'].isin(max_depts)) & (employees['position'] == 'Manager')]
    res = managers[['emp_name', 'dep_id']].rename(columns={'emp_name': 'manager_name'})
    return res.sort_values(by='dep_id')
